title: What happens if you never get out of bed?

qwen_instruct.narrator: Punchy, dramatic storyteller, fast and confident, building suspense.
qwen_instruct.doctor: Calm, deep, slightly dry American hospital doctor.
qwen_instruct.gary: Cocky, cheerful young man, very sure of himself.

lines.text: Three weeks in bed will wreck your body worse than thirty years of getting old.
Day one. No alarm. No stairs. Snacks in reach. Bliss.
In 1966, scientists in Dallas did this to five fit twenty-year-olds.
Three weeks, flat on their backs.
Your blood drops to your feet, and the room spins.
On the treadmill, their fitness had crashed by more than a quarter.
Every heartbeat pushed out almost a third less blood.
Stay longer, and your bones thin by about one percent a month.
NASA once offered eighteen thousand dollars to lie in bed for seventy days, just to study it.
Thirty years later, the same men came back.
Three decades of ageing had hurt their fitness less than those three weeks in bed.
But here's the twist. Back in 1966, eight weeks of training made them fitter than before.
That's why heart patients, once kept in bed for weeks, now get up within days.
So get up. Your heart is counting. Comment what you want to know next.

experiment.note: Remake of 014 in the new set-video style: several 3D sets (bedroom, 1966 Dallas lab, treadmill, heart/X-ray, NASA tilt bed, 1996 reunion, 1950s ward, morning street), a cut about every 2 s, character lines in other voices, recorded CC0 SFX. Hypothesis: fast cuts + a hard number hook hold retention better than 014's slow cel version.

facts.claim: Dallas Bed Rest and Training Study (1966): five healthy 20-year-old men, 3 weeks strict bed rest; VO2max fell 27%, maximal stroke volume fell 31%; 8 weeks of training then raised VO2max 45% (above the pre-bed-rest level)
30-year follow-up: the decline in VO2max from age 20 to 50 was smaller than after 3 weeks of bed rest at 20
The study helped end weeks of strict bed rest for heart-attack patients in favour of early mobilisation and cardiac rehab
After bed rest, standing up often causes dizziness or fainting (orthostatic intolerance) as blood pools in the legs
Bed rest / unloading bone loss is roughly 1% (to 1.5%) per month
NASA's 70-day 6-degree head-down bed rest study (2013) offered $18,000
